newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to sell 22 military plants this year.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to sell 22 military plants this year.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet decided on Monday to sell 22 military industrial plants by year-end under an ambitious privatisation plan aimed to boost the balance of payments, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
"The 22 arms plants are part of the government's list of enterprises for speedy privatisation," Bozhkov told reporters after a cabinet meeting. He did not elaborate.

Bulgaria will rely mostly on privatisation proceeds to fund a budget deficit of 6.2 percent of GDP, after the government introduces a restrictive monetary mechanism known as a currency board on July 1.

Previous governments, reluctant to privatise some 100 plants comprising Bulgaria's once flourishing military industry, imposed a ban on their privatisation. The majority of the plants make components and can easily be converted to other production.

Bulgaria's transition to a market economy, the collapse of traditional markets and arms trade embargoes have caused losses for the arms plants since the collapse of the communist regime seven years ago.

Bozhkov said that by the end of the year, the government aimed to sell off a further 70 major state-owned plants, which include the Neftochim oil refinery, Chimco chemical plant, pharmaceutical plants Pharmacia, Troyapharm and Sopharma, several metal smelters and the Bourgas and Rousse shipyards.
He said the government planned to sell a grand total of 583 firms this year including small enterprises, and hoped to receive 602 billion levs. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
